title: AI Gateways — LiteLLM, Portkey, Kong AI Gateway, Bifrost

questions.question: What is the core role of an AI gateway in the lesson?
options: A model fine-tuning service that trains custom LoRA adapters on top of a base model
A process sitting between apps and model providers that consolidates routing, fallback, retries, rate limits, secret references, observability, and guardrails behind one API
A vector database for retrieval that stores embeddings for RAG pipelines
A logging-only sidecar that records requests and responses without touching routing or fallback
questions.explanation: The lesson defines an AI gateway as a process sitting between apps and model providers that consolidates provider routing, fallback, retries, rate limits, secret references, observability, and guardrails behind one typically OpenAI-compatible API.

questions.question: What scale ceiling does Kong's benchmark report for LiteLLM?
options: It tops out at 50 RPS, far below the figure the lesson attributes to Kong's published benchmark
It scales linearly past 10k RPS with no reported memory or failure issues at that volume
It breaks down around ~2000 RPS with 8 GB memory and cascading failures under sustained load
LiteLLM cannot be benchmarked because it has no fixed request-per-second ceiling to measure
questions.explanation: The lesson reports that in published benchmarks LiteLLM breaks down around ~2000 RPS, with an 8 GB memory footprint and cascading failures under sustained load, making it best suited to Python apps under 500 RPS rather than large-scale production.

questions.question: Per the Kong benchmark on equivalent CPU, how much faster is Kong AI Gateway than Portkey and LiteLLM?
options: About 10% and 20% faster, a modest edge rather than the multiple Kong's benchmark actually claims
Identical performance to both Portkey and LiteLLM on Kong's own published benchmark numbers
Slower than both Portkey and LiteLLM, according to Kong's own published benchmark numbers
228% faster than Portkey and 859% faster than LiteLLM
questions.explanation: The lesson cites Kong's own benchmark claiming 228% faster than Portkey and 859% faster than LiteLLM on equivalent CPU -- while also flagging that vendor self-benchmarks are marketing material and should be re-measured on your own traffic.

questions.question: Which gateway does the lesson position with 20-40 ms latency overhead and guardrails / PII redaction / jailbreak detection focus?
options: Portkey — MIT-licensed control plane with guardrails, PII redaction, and jailbreak detection
Kong AI Gateway — built on Kong Gateway, priced per model per month, the scale play
LiteLLM — MIT OSS router for 100+ providers, breaks down near 2000 RPS in published benchmarks
Cloudflare AI Gateway — managed, zero-ops, basic retry and observability at the edge
questions.explanation: The lesson positions Portkey as a control-plane product focused on guardrails, PII redaction, jailbreak detection, and audit trails, with a 20-40 ms per-request latency overhead -- best fit for regulated industries. Portkey is MIT-licensed open source since 2024.

questions.question: What does the lesson say is the forcing function for self-hosted vs managed gateway decisions?
options: Whether the gateway is open source, since the lesson treats license alone as the deciding factor
Data residency requirements — healthcare and finance default to self-host, consumer products default managed
Number of supported providers, since more provider coverage always favors a self-hosted deployment
Cost per request, since the lesson ranks gateways purely by per-call pricing rather than by deployment model at all
questions.explanation: The lesson states data residency is the forcing function: healthcare and finance default to self-host (LiteLLM, Portkey OSS, or Kong), consumer products default to managed or middle-tier options, and regulated tenants can be split hybrid.

questions.question: Which gateways stay within budget when the SLA is TTFT P99 < 100 ms?
options: Any gateway, since the lesson treats all four latency-overhead figures as interchangeable at that SLA
Only Portkey, whose 20-40 ms overhead the lesson treats as the tightest budget fit for that SLA
Kong (~3-8 ms) or Cloudflare/Vercel edge gateways (~1-3 ms); Portkey at 20-40 ms is too heavy
Only LiteLLM, whose 5-15 ms overhead the lesson treats as the sole fit for that SLA
questions.explanation: The lesson's latency budget table gives Kong ~3-8 ms and Cloudflare/Vercel ~1-3 ms overhead versus Portkey's 20-40 ms, and states that for a TTFT P99 < 100 ms SLA, Kong or Cloudflare/Vercel fit while Portkey is too heavy.
